mindtraced_atomic_units: The PS/2 mouse protocol sends messages that are three bytes long.
The first byte of each message has in[3]=1.
A finite state machine (FSM) is required to identify message boundaries.
The FSM discards bytes until it detects a byte with in[3]=1.
The FSM assumes this byte is the first of a message and waits for two more bytes.
The FSM signals 'done' immediately after receiving the third byte.
The reset signal is active high and synchronous.
spec_atomic_units: The module is defined as module top_module (input clk, input [7:0] in, input reset, output done).
The 'in' input is an 8-bit data stream where in[3] indicates the start of a message.
The 'reset' input is active high and synchronous.
The 'done' output signals the successful receipt of a complete message.
The FSM detects the start of a message when in[3]=1.
A counter tracks the number of bytes received since the last message start.
The counter increments with each byte received.
The 'done' output is asserted when the counter reaches 3.
The FSM resets the counter when in[3]=1.
The FSM operates on the rising edge of 'clk'.
